summary: Targeted primary-filing archaeology materially narrows four active-batch blockers without changing canonical state. CRDO concentration/dilution is now quantitatively bounded from the FY2026 10-K; ALAB fully diluted overhang and governance concentration are quantified from the FY2025 10-K/proxy; ARM related-party/customer concentration is quantified from the FY2026 20-F; VRT backlog quality is bounded from the FY2025 10-K but customer concentration remains unresolved. Chief should review/corroborate before promotion.

targets.researchQuestion: Can FY2026 primary filings quantify customer concentration, contracting fragility and current equity dilution enough to close the active-batch blocker?
targets.summary: Primary evidence materially closes the quantitative concentration and dilution portions of the gate. FY2026 end-customer concentration is extreme: Customer A represented 49% of revenue and Customer B 32%; top-10 customers were ~90%. At May 2, 2026, Customer A represented 53% of accounts receivable, Customer B 20%, Customer C 19%. Contracts are predominantly purchase-order based with no general long-term minimum commitments and can be cancelled/changed/delayed subject to negotiated terms. Equity overhang remains material but measurable: 185.4M ordinary shares outstanding at May 2, 2026 plus options/RSUs covering 10.8M shares (~5.8% of then-outstanding shares before treasury-stock effects); FY2026 diluted weighted-average shares were 188.232M versus 178.538M basic. FY2026 share-based compensation was $182.638M. The company also issued 4.820M shares through an ATM for $736.327M net and 3.761M shares on exercise of a customer warrant during FY2026.

findings.claim: FY2026 Customer A = 49% of revenue, Customer B = 32%; top-10 customers ~90%.
At May 2, 2026 A/R concentration: Customer A 53%, B 20%, C 19%.
185.4M shares outstanding at May 2, 2026 and 10.8M option/RSU shares outstanding; 186.478M shares outstanding June 8, 2026.
FY2026 SBC $182.638M; ATM issued 4.820M shares for $736.327M net; customer warrant exercise issued 3.761M shares.
Concentration risk is not merely generic hyperscaler exposure; two end customers drove ~81% of FY2026 revenue, so durability of those deployments is a first-order underwriting variable.

unknowns: Public filing labels customers A/B rather than naming the end customers; identity mapping should remain unknown unless independently sourced.
Durability beyond FY2026 is not proven by one year of concentration data.
falsifiers: Material diversification of revenue/A/R in subsequent filings would weaken concentration-risk severity.
Long-term non-cancellable customer commitments found in customer-specific primary contracts would weaken purchase-order fragility inference.

targets.exactGate: fully diluted share-count roll-forward and governance; true end-customer mapping remains separate
targets.researchQuestion: Can the 2025 10-K and 2026 proxy reconcile current equity overhang and governance concentration?
targets.summary: Primary filings materially close the dilution/governance part of the gate. At Dec. 31, 2025 Astera had 2.721M options, 9.531M RSU/PSU awards and 2.442M warrants outstanding, totaling 14.695M gross potential shares before forfeiture/exercise/treasury-stock effects. The 2026 proxy reports 171.247M common shares outstanding at March 1 and 171.282M at April 13, implying the disclosed gross overhang equals ~8.6% of the March 1 base if all listed instruments ultimately issue one share each. FY2025 SBC expense was $160.0M. The 2024 equity plan also permits annual reserve increases up to 5% of prior-year outstanding shares, while the ESPP can increase by the lesser of 3.091M shares, 1% of prior-year outstanding shares or a compensation-committee-set lower amount. Executive officers, directors and >5% holders collectively beneficially owned ~37.9% as of Dec. 31, 2025 under the 10-K disclosure; the proxy should be used for person-level ownership details. Governance is therefore concentrated but not dual-class in the cited material.

findings.claim: 2.721M options + 9.531M RSU/PSU + 2.442M warrants outstanding at Dec. 31, 2025 = 14.695M gross potential shares.
171.247M common shares outstanding March 1, 2026; 171.282M at April 13, 2026.
FY2025 SBC expense $160.0M; directors/officers/>5% holders collectively ~37.9% of outstanding common stock at Dec. 31, 2025 under 10-K disclosure.
2024 Plan annual reserve can increase by up to 5% of prior-year outstanding shares; ESPP annual increase has a 1%/3.091M/lower-board-choice cap.

Gross disclosed option/RSU/PSU/warrant overhang is ~8.6% of the March 1, 2026 share base before treasury-stock effects and future grants; use as an upper-bound style dilution indicator, not a forecast of actual issued shares.

unknowns: True end-customer mapping remains unresolved and must not be inferred from warrant counterparty or channel data.
A clean fully diluted denominator still requires instrument-level vesting/exercise assumptions and avoidance of double-counting awards already reflected in diluted weighted-average shares.
falsifiers: Subsequent filings showing large forfeitures, cash settlement or non-exercisable awards would reduce gross overhang.
A later cap-table filing supersedes March/April 2026 share counts.

targets.exactGate: related-party economics, SoftBank/control governance and customer concentration
targets.researchQuestion: Can FY2026 primary filing evidence quantify related-party economics and concentration without guessing customer identities?
targets.summary: FY2026 20-F materially closes the related-party and concentration quantification. Related-party revenue was $1.499B of $4.920B total (~30.5%), up 82% year over year from $823M, driven primarily by a $591M increase in related-party license/other revenue and $85M increase in related-party royalty revenue. Top five customers including Arm China and SoftBank Group collectively represented ~57% of FY2026 revenue; Arm China alone represented ~16%. Mobile application processors still constituted ~43% of FY2026 royalty revenue. The filing explicitly states a portion of near-term revenue depends on commercial arrangements with SoftBank Group and affiliates. This is enough to treat related-party exposure and customer concentration as material underwriting inputs, but not enough by itself to conclude transactions are non-arm's-length or economically adverse.

findings.claim: FY2026 related-party revenue $1.499B versus $823M FY2025; total FY2026 revenue $4.920B.
Top five customers including Arm China and SoftBank Group were ~57% of FY2026 revenue; Arm China ~16%.
Mobile application processors were ~43% of FY2026 royalty revenue; near-term revenue partly depends on SoftBank Group/affiliate commercial arrangements.
Related-party dependence is economically material (~30.5% of FY2026 revenue), so governance/control analysis should explicitly separate SoftBank strategic demand from diversified third-party demand.

unknowns: This artifact does not establish whether SoftBank-related pricing is above/below independent market terms.
SoftBank control/voting mechanics should be corroborated from the latest ownership/proxy-style filing before the governance gate is considered complete.
falsifiers: A later filing showing related-party revenue falling to immaterial levels would reduce this risk.
Independent contract benchmarking proving ordinary commercial terms would weaken concern about economic dependence while not eliminating concentration.

targets.exactGate: customer concentration plus backlog aging/cancellation quality
targets.researchQuestion: How firm is the reported backlog, what is its expected conversion horizon, and what cancellation/aging risks does the primary filing disclose?
targets.summary: The FY2025 10-K materially closes backlog definition and cancellation-quality semantics but not named/quantified customer concentration. Backlog was ~$15.0B at Dec. 31, 2025 versus ~$7.2B a year earlier. It consists of products/services with a customer purchase order or purchase commitment not yet delivered. The majority is considered firm and expected to ship within 12-18 months. However, customers can in some circumstances reduce or defer firm orders, generally with penalties or other termination consequences; acquired businesses can have different termination rights. Vertiv explicitly warns backlog is not guaranteed revenue. Compared with FY2024, the expected majority-conversion horizon lengthened from within one year to 12-18 months, which is a useful aging/lead-time signal and should be tested against subsequent quarterly conversion rather than automatically treated as deterioration.

findings.claim: Backlog ~$15.0B at Dec. 31, 2025 vs ~$7.2B at Dec. 31, 2024; majority considered firm, expected delivery 12-18 months.
Customers may in some circumstances reduce/defer firm orders, usually with penalties or termination consequences; acquisition contracts may have differing cancellation rights.
FY2024 filing described majority of backlog as expected within one year; FY2025 filing uses 12-18 months.
The horizon extension may reflect larger/longer AI infrastructure programs, lead times, acquisition mix or aging; it is a monitoring flag, not evidence of cancellation by itself.

unknowns: No sufficiently specific primary disclosure found in this pass to quantify top-customer concentration.
Backlog cancellation rate, reschedule rate and aging buckets are not disclosed in the cited filing.
Acquisition-added backlog should be separated from organic backlog growth if Chief needs a clean durability measure.
falsifiers: Subsequent filings showing rapid backlog conversion with stable cancellations would weaken backlog-aging concern.
Material backlog reductions not explained by revenue conversion would strengthen cancellation/quality concern.
